parameters.content:
## Collections / Reminders - Stock Template

Daily branch that checks Xero for outstanding (AUTHORISED, AmountDue > 0, ACCREC) invoices and escalates by days past DueDate:
- 7+ days overdue -> Reminder 1 (gentle)
- 14+ days overdue -> Reminder 2 (firmer)
- 21+ days overdue -> Reminder 3 (firm) AND flagged for manual follow-up

Only the highest stage currently reached is sent per run (a missed run doesn't fire all three reminders in one go retroactively) - each invoice only ever gets one email per stage.

### Credentials
Reuses the exact same Xero (`4p323BIqqLPBGyHS`) and Resend (`YHY8OwE9VDR10sYO`) credentials already wired into the main Invoice Automation workflow. No new credentials or integrations added.

### Dedup / stage tracking - chosen approach: Xero Invoice History
Each invoice's reminder progress is tracked via tagged entries on that invoice's own Xero History (`PUT /Invoices/{id}/History`, `Details: "COLLECTIONS_STAGE=N ..."`) - read back on every run (`GET /Invoices/{id}/History`) to compute the highest stage already sent. Chosen over a new Google Sheet or new credential specifically because the brief said to reuse only the existing Xero + Resend auth with no new setup - this keeps the tracking entirely inside Xero's own audit trail on the invoice, nothing external to stand up or share access to.

### Manual follow-up flag (21+ days) - chosen approach: both
At stage 3, in addition to the client-facing Reminder 3 email, this: (a) writes a second tagged Xero History entry (`COLLECTIONS_FLAGGED_FOR_MANUAL_FOLLOWUP`) so it's permanently visible on the invoice's own audit trail, AND (b) sends an internal notification email via Resend to a new `collectionsNotificationEmail` Client Config field. Reasoning: a note nobody actively checks isn't really a flag - the email actively surfaces it to a person, while the History entry makes the flag itself idempotent and auditable on the invoice.

### Three triggers, same as every other workflow in this project
- Schedule Trigger: real production path, daily.
- Manual Trigger + "Sample Mock Invoices": click-to-test in the editor with 5 built-in fake invoices covering all four overdue states (not due / 7+ / 14+ / 21+) plus a dedup case (still 8 days overdue, already got Reminder 1 - must NOT resend).
- Webhook (POST /webhook/invoice/collections-check): accepts `{ testMode: true, testInvoices: [...] }` to run the exact same escalation logic against custom fake invoices via API - this is what was used for the pre-live test run (see README). `testMode: true` bypasses the real Xero invoice fetch AND skips the real Xero History write (so testing never touches real Xero data), but still sends real Resend emails so delivery is actually proven, not just simulated.

See workflows/invoice-automation/README.md for full test results and flagged parameter-shape uncertainties (Xero History HTTP method, multi-condition `where` filter, `summaryOnly=false`, daily Schedule Trigger shape) - all unverified against real Xero data, same caveat as every other native-node integration in this project on first build.

nodes.name: Schedule Trigger (daily 08:00)
nodes.notes: Parameter-shape flag: the 'days' field/triggerAtHour shape here is my best-effort recollection of n8n's Schedule Trigger schema, only the 'minutes' field type has actually been proven live in this project (Sheet Poller). Verify the first scheduled run actually fires at 08:00 as expected.

nodes.name: Sample Mock Invoices (Manual Test)
nodes.notes: 5 fixtures covering all four overdue states plus one explicit duplicate-prevention case (invoice E: still 8 days overdue, already sent Reminder 1 - must NOT resend). Dates computed relative to 'now' so this stays valid whenever it's run.

const body = $json.body || {};
return [{ json: { testMode: !!body.testMode, testInvoices: Array.isArray(body.testInvoices) ? body.testInvoices : [] } }];

const config = $input.item.json;
const invoices = config.testInvoices || [];
return invoices.map(inv => ({
  json: {
    invoiceId: inv.invoiceId,
    invoiceNumber: inv.invoiceNumber,
    contactName: inv.contactName,
    contactEmail: inv.contactEmail,
    dueDate: inv.dueDate,
    amountDue: Number(inv.amountDue) || 0,
    currencyCode: inv.currencyCode || 'GBP',
    alreadySentStage: Number(inv.alreadySentStage) || 0,
    testMode: true,
    source: 'test',
    clientId: config.clientId,
    clientName: config.clientName,
    brandColour: config.brandColour,
    paymentOptions: config.paymentOptions,
    confirmationFromEmail: config.confirmationFromEmail,
    collectionsNotificationEmail: config.collectionsNotificationEmail,
    collectionsReminder1Days: config.collectionsReminder1Days,
    collectionsReminder2Days: config.collectionsReminder2Days,
    collectionsReminder3Days: config.collectionsReminder3Days,
  }
}));

nodes.name: Xero - Get Outstanding Invoices
nodes.notes: Parameter-shape flag: multi-condition 'where' with && and summaryOnly=false are both my best-effort recollection of Xero's query syntax - only single-condition where clauses (Reference==, Name==) have actually been proven live in this project. Verify this returns the expected set on the first live run.

const resp = $input.item.json;
const prior = $('Extract Tenant ID').item.json;

return invoices.map(inv => ({

    invoiceId: inv.InvoiceID,
    invoiceNumber: inv.InvoiceNumber,
    contactId: inv.Contact ? inv.Contact.ContactID : null,
    contactName: inv.Contact ? inv.Contact.Name : null,
    contactEmail: inv.Contact ? (inv.Contact.EmailAddress || '') : '',
    dueDate: (inv.DueDateString || '').slice(0, 10),
    amountDue: inv.AmountDue,
    currencyCode: inv.CurrencyCode,
    testMode: false,
    source: 'live',
    xeroTenantId: prior.xeroTenantId,
    clientId: prior.clientId,
    clientName: prior.clientName,
    brandColour: prior.brandColour,
    paymentOptions: prior.paymentOptions,
    confirmationFromEmail: prior.confirmationFromEmail,
    collectionsNotificationEmail: prior.collectionsNotificationEmail,
    collectionsReminder1Days: prior.collectionsReminder1Days,
    collectionsReminder2Days: prior.collectionsReminder2Days,
    collectionsReminder3Days: prior.collectionsReminder3Days,
  }
}));

nodes.name: Xero - Get Contact Email
nodes.notes: The Invoices list response's embedded Contact object may not include EmailAddress even with summaryOnly=false - this fetches the full Contact record per invoice to be sure a real address is available before emailing. Flagging as unverified against real overdue invoices.

nodes.name: Compute Days Overdue + Target Stage
nodes.notes: Shared by both the test and live branches. Only sends when targetStage > alreadySentStage - so an invoice still at 8 days overdue after already receiving Reminder 1 (targetStage=1, alreadySentStage=1) correctly does NOT resend. A missed run (e.g. invoice jumps straight to 25 days overdue with nothing sent yet) sends only Reminder 3, not a backlog of 1+2+3.

nodes.name: Is Stage 1?
nodes.notes: Cascaded IF nodes (Stage 1? -> else Stage 2? -> else must be Stage 3) used instead of a Switch node - the IF node's parameter shape has already been proven working repeatedly in this project; Switch has not been used anywhere yet, so this avoids introducing an unproven node type for a 3-way branch that only needs 2 checks anyway.

nodes.notes: Resend API - POST /emails. Uses the 'Header Auth account 2' credential, same as the main workflow's confirmation email.

nodes.notes: Resend API - POST /emails. Uses the 'Header Auth account 2' credential.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ from: $json.confirmationFromEmail, to: [$json.collectionsNotificationEmail], subject: `[Action needed] Invoice ${$json.invoiceNumber} - ${$json.daysOverdue} days overdue, flagged for follow-up`, text: `Invoice ${$json.invoiceNumber} (Xero ID ${$json.invoiceId}) for ${$json.contactName} is now ${$json.daysOverdue} days overdue (amount due: ${$json.currencyCode} ${$json.amountDue}).\n\nThis has crossed the ${$json.collectionsReminder3Days || 21}-day threshold and has been flagged for manual follow-up. The client-facing Reminder 3 email has already been sent to ${$json.contactEmail}.` }) }}

nodes.name: Send Manual Follow-up Notification (Resend)
nodes.notes: Internal notification, not customer-facing - sent to Client Config's collectionsNotificationEmail. This is the 'flag for manual follow-up' requirement, paired with the COLLECTIONS_FLAGGED_FOR_MANUAL_FOLLOWUP Xero History entry written a few nodes downstream.

nodes.name: Record Reminder 3 Sent + Flagged
nodes.notes: References $('Is Stage 2?') deliberately - that's the last node before this branch that still carried the full invoice item (targetStage=2 FALSE output means 'must be stage 3', it does not mean this item's own targetStage is 2).

nodes.name: Skip Xero Write (Test Mode)
nodes.notes: Test-mode invoice IDs (TEST-INV-A etc.) don't exist in real Xero, so writing History against them would just 404 - skipped here, historyNote is preserved on the item for inspection in the test summary instead of being written anywhere.

nodes.name: Xero - Write History Record
nodes.notes: Parameter-shape flag: PUT is Xero's documented pattern for creating History/Notes entries on Invoices (same as Contacts, CreditNotes, etc.), but this exact call is unverified against real Xero data in this project - if the first live run 404s or 405s, this is the first thing to check (method PUT vs POST, and whether InvoiceID needs to be a real AUTHORISED invoice with actual history already, which it will be for any live-fetched invoice).
